faqs.q: What is the main difference between freelancing and entrepreneurship?
faqs.a: A freelancer sells their own skills and time to clients, so income depends on the work they personally do. An entrepreneur builds a business that sells products or services and can grow beyond one person's effort through a team, systems and investment.

faqs.q: Is freelancing less risky than starting a business?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Freelancing needs little or no upfront investment and you can start earning fairly quickly, while a business often needs capital and time before it becomes profitable and can fail. Freelancing has its own risk, though, because work and income depend on finding clients consistently.

faqs.q: Is freelancing or entrepreneurship better for students?
faqs.a: Freelancing usually suits students better at the start, because it needs little money, fits around classes and builds real skills and a portfolio. Students with a strong business idea can still try entrepreneurship, but should be ready for slower returns and more uncertainty.

faqs.q: Can a freelancer turn their work into a business?
faqs.a: Yes, many entrepreneurs start as freelancers. A common route is to gain experience and clients, save money, build a recognisable brand and then hire people or create products so the work no longer depends only on your own hours, for example by growing a freelance service into an agency.
